v.rationale: impl-2 is the most correct. Its job only sends rows that are still claimed, so SQS redelivery does not resend. It caps Retry-After, uses FailOnTimeout, records the claim time as synced_at, and has the strongest Pest suite. Its main weaknesses are a roundabout claim (update, then re-select by timestamp) and no withoutOverlapping. impl-1 has good 429 handling (tooManyRequests, capped delay) and a locked claim, but its job re-sends on redelivery. It also uses raw SQL with an interpolated date, makes the sync columns mass-assignable, adds an invented rate limiter, deleted the base example tests, and has an idempotency test that cannot fail. impl-3 has the cleanest claim code but uses Retry-After without a cap. A large value holds the job far past the 15-minute claim, which causes a duplicate send, and the late failure then clears the newer claim. It also re-sends on redelivery, gives up at minute 14 with a 60s timeout (too close to the cutoff), and tests the 429 path with Mockery instead of the fake queue helpers. All three lose an edit made in the same second as the claim, and all three let a late failed() clear a newer claim; since these are shared, they do not affect the ranking.
